publishingPolicy: Export creates scheduling files only. Every post requires a human brand, exam-accuracy, privacy, and rights review before platform scheduling.
privacyPolicy: Illustrative demos must be visibly labeled. A real transcript, voice, score, image, or learner story may replace a demo only after written, purpose-specific, revocable consent is recorded.

posts.sourceConsentRequirement: Default to a fictional demo answer. A real learner transcript or audio requires written consent naming TikTok, the exact excerpt, score context, and publication period.
posts.disclosure: Show 'Illustrative demo — not a real learner' on screen for the full transcript segment.
posts.hook: Your transcript is not the feedback. This is.
posts.caption: Highlight one repeated phrase, one abandoned sentence, and one pause pattern. Then retry the same IELTS prompt with only one target. That turns a transcript into a practice decision.
posts.cta: Use the free score diagnostic from the SpeakAce link in bio.
posts.assetBrief: Split screen: fictional transcript on the left, three annotated patterns on the right, then a one-line retry goal.

posts.sourceConsentRequirement: Use fictional student data by default. Any real class or learner example requires written learner consent and, where applicable, institution approval before publication.
posts.disclosure: Label the example 'Illustrative demo data' on slides 1 and 5.
posts.hook: A transcript becomes useful only when it changes the next attempt.
posts.caption: For teachers, the useful workflow is short: evidence, one priority, same-prompt retry, comparison. The goal is not more feedback text. It is a clearer next practice decision.
posts.cta: Open the SpeakAce teacher demo to see the workflow.
posts.assetBrief: Five slides: answer, evidence, priority, retry, teacher follow-up. Use no names or realistic profile details.

posts.sourceConsentRequirement: Use a fictional answer. Publishing a real transcript, score, photo, or handle requires written channel-specific consent and a documented removal path.
posts.disclosure: Add 'Illustrative demo' to every slide containing an answer or score.
posts.hook: Diagnose one answer in four checks.
posts.caption: Fluency: long pauses. Vocabulary: repeated general words. Grammar: abandoned sentences. Pronunciation: missing stress on meaning words. Pick the weakest category and retry once.
posts.cta: Save this checklist, then request the full diagnostic from our bio.
posts.assetBrief: Six clean slides: cover, four criterion checks, final 10-minute retry card.

posts.sourceConsentRequirement: No learner source is used. Exam-accuracy review is still required; do not imply affiliation with IELTS test owners.
posts.disclosure: No learner claim. Add 'Independent practice guidance' if a branded visual is used.
posts.hook: Test-day confidence is usually evidence accumulated before test day.
posts.caption: A useful weekly routine is one timed answer, one evidence-based review, and one same-prompt retry. Learners arrive calmer when they have seen their own pattern improve—not because they memorized more generic advice.
posts.cta: Try one free scored speaking attempt.
posts.assetBrief: Optional typographic quote card with no exam-owner marks.

posts.sourceConsentRequirement: No learner source is used. A presenter must approve use of their image and voice; exam guidance requires editorial review.
posts.disclosure: Caption as independent practice guidance; make no score guarantee.
posts.hook: Lost your sentence? Do this instead of apologizing.
posts.caption: Pause, finish the idea with a shorter sentence, and continue. A clear recovery is more useful than repeating the same broken sentence three times.
posts.cta: Practice a calm recovery before test day.
posts.assetBrief: Presenter demonstrates a tangled sentence, calm reset, then clean continuation with on-screen steps.

posts.sourceConsentRequirement: Use scripted demo audio and text. Real before/after attempts require written consent for both clips, score context, and Instagram reuse.
posts.disclosure: Show 'Scripted illustrative retry' throughout the before/after comparison.
posts.hook: Do not change the prompt on your second attempt.
posts.caption: Keep the same question and ideas. Improve one criterion. That is how you can actually see what changed between attempt one and attempt two.
posts.cta: Save this for your next score-and-retry session.
posts.assetBrief: Scripted before/after waveform with the single changed target highlighted.

posts.sourceConsentRequirement: Use a fictional transcript and scripted voice. A real recording requires explicit written consent covering audio, transcript, inferred feedback, and TikTok publication.
posts.disclosure: Show 'Illustrative demo' while any transcript or feedback is visible.
posts.hook: Three tiny transcript marks can reveal your fluency pattern.
posts.caption: Mark long pauses, restarts, and filler clusters. Do not delete every pause; practice replacing one repeated restart with a clean sentence opening.
posts.cta: Get a transcript and one next step with free practice.
posts.assetBrief: Animated fictional transcript with pause, restart, and filler symbols appearing in sequence.

posts.sourceConsentRequirement: No learner source is used. Any later classroom metric must be aggregated, de-identified, consented where required, and approved by the institution.
posts.disclosure: Diagram is a proposed practice model, not measured learner outcomes.
posts.hook: More feedback is not always more teachable.
posts.caption: A learner can act on one priority today. A practical feedback stack is evidence from the answer, one scoring category, one concrete exercise, and a same-prompt retry. Everything else can wait.
posts.cta: Explore the class feedback workflow in the teacher demo.
posts.assetBrief: Simple four-stage loop diagram labeled proposed workflow.

posts.sourceConsentRequirement: Script all voice and transcript content. Real learner material requires written, Instagram-specific consent and approval of the final edit.
posts.disclosure: On-screen label: 'Scripted fluency demo'.
posts.hook: A faster answer is not automatically a more fluent answer.
posts.caption: Keep a natural pace. On the retry, focus on fewer restarts and cleaner links between ideas—not racing the timer.
posts.cta: Try the same prompt twice and compare.
posts.assetBrief: Two scripted waveforms: rushed version versus calm connected version; avoid numeric score claims.

posts.sourceConsentRequirement: Use fictional roster and attempt data. Real student work requires written learner consent plus teacher or institution authorization for LinkedIn publication.
posts.disclosure: Label all roster and score views 'Illustrative demo data'.
posts.hook: A better speaking assignment includes the retry before the learner begins.
posts.caption: Set the prompt, the timing, the single review question, and the retry target together. The learner knows what evidence to look for before submitting attempt one.
posts.cta: Use the teacher demo to map your next assignment.
posts.assetBrief: Four slides showing a fictional assignment from prompt to retry review.

posts.sourceConsentRequirement: No learner source is used. Presenter image and voice rights plus exam-accuracy approval are required.
posts.disclosure: Independent preparation tip; do not use official IELTS marks or imply endorsement.
posts.hook: Your Part 2 notes need only four anchors.
posts.caption: Write person or thing, moment, detail, and why it matters. Four anchors are easier to speak from than eight full sentences you try to memorize.
posts.cta: Practice turning four anchors into one timed answer.
posts.assetBrief: Overhead shot of four-word note plan becoming a simple spoken outline.

posts.sourceConsentRequirement: No learner material is used. Editorial exam review is required before scheduling.
posts.disclosure: No outcome claim; present as a practice routine.
posts.hook: Not every pause is a fluency problem.
posts.caption: Useful pause: between complete ideas. Costly pause: repeatedly restarting the same unfinished sentence. Practice finishing a shorter sentence before adding detail.
posts.cta: Save the pause checklist for your next recording.
posts.assetBrief: Five typographic slides contrasting useful and costly pauses with original examples.

posts.sourceConsentRequirement: Use fictional transcript text. A real learner excerpt requires written consent for the text, feedback annotation, and TikTok distribution.
posts.disclosure: Label transcript 'Illustrative demo'.
posts.hook: Stop replacing every simple word in your transcript.
posts.caption: Find the two general words you repeat most. Replace only those with precise, natural choices. Vocabulary range is not a synonym contest.
posts.cta: Run one transcript check and retry.
posts.assetBrief: Fictional transcript where only two repeated words change; all other text remains stable.

posts.sourceConsentRequirement: No learner example is needed. If one is added, anonymization alone is insufficient; obtain written consent for the exact use and preserve withdrawal instructions.
posts.disclosure: State clearly whether any future example is illustrative or consented and anonymized.
posts.hook: Removing a learner's name does not automatically make a transcript publishable.
posts.caption: Voice, topic details, timing, and score history can still identify someone. Public feedback examples need purpose-specific consent, data minimization, a final-edit review, and a removal path. Otherwise, use a clearly labeled illustrative demo.
posts.cta: Use the privacy-safe teacher demo for product evaluation.
posts.assetBrief: Optional checklist visual: consent, minimize, review, remove.

posts.sourceConsentRequirement: All example answer text must be fictional. Real answers or scores require written consent and final carousel approval from the learner.
posts.disclosure: Mark answer excerpts 'Illustrative demo'.
posts.hook: One reason plus one example can rescue a thin answer.
posts.caption: Do not add five disconnected points. On your retry, keep the main answer, explain one reason, and give one specific example. Development becomes clearer without sounding memorized.
posts.cta: Save the reason-example retry formula.
posts.assetBrief: Five slides transform a fictional thin answer into a reason-and-example structure without assigning a numeric score.

posts.sourceConsentRequirement: Use fictional, non-realistic roster data. Real class analytics require institutional authorization, appropriate written learner consent, aggregation, and suppression of small cohorts.
posts.disclosure: Every analytics slide must say 'Illustrative demo data'.
posts.hook: A useful class dashboard should answer: who needs what next?
posts.caption: Start with overdue practice, weakest category, recent direction, and the next assigned action. Reporting is valuable when it shortens the teacher's decision—not when it creates another spreadsheet.
posts.cta: Walk through the illustrative class in the SpeakAce teacher demo.
posts.assetBrief: Five privacy-safe fictional dashboard slides with no realistic names or claims of live customer use.

posts.sourceConsentRequirement: No learner source is used. Presenter rights and exam-accuracy review are required.
posts.disclosure: Independent practice advice; no official affiliation or score promise.
posts.hook: Do not know much about the topic? Narrow the answer.
posts.caption: Choose one familiar angle, answer it directly, and explain why. You are demonstrating communication, not specialist knowledge.
posts.cta: Practice an unfamiliar topic with a simple angle.
posts.assetBrief: Presenter receives an unfamiliar fictional topic and models a one-angle outline.

posts.sourceConsentRequirement: Use scripted voice and fictional transcript. A real before/after example needs written consent for both versions and the feedback framing.
posts.disclosure: Show 'Scripted illustrative retry' during both clips.
posts.hook: The stronger retry changes two words, not twenty.
posts.caption: Precision beats forced complexity. Keep the sentence natural and upgrade the repeated words that actually blur your meaning.
posts.cta: Try a two-word vocabulary retry today.
posts.assetBrief: Scripted before/after where two highlighted choices become more precise.

posts.sourceConsentRequirement: Use scripted audio. Real learner voice or pronunciation feedback requires explicit written consent for audio, transcript, analysis, and TikTok use.
posts.disclosure: Label audio and transcript 'Scripted demo'.
posts.hook: Your transcript cannot show this pronunciation problem by itself.
posts.caption: Read the sentence once with every word equally strong, then again stressing the meaning words. Pair the transcript with audio; pronunciation evidence is not text-only.
posts.cta: Record, listen, and retry one sentence.
posts.assetBrief: Scripted audio with stress bars moving from flat to meaning-focused; no accent judgment.

posts.sourceConsentRequirement: No learner data is used. Any product screenshot must contain approved fictional data or separately consented material.
posts.disclosure: Describe AI output as practice feedback, not an official IELTS result.
posts.hook: AI feedback should make its evidence boundary visible.
posts.caption: A responsible speaking tool distinguishes practice estimates from official scores, ties suggestions to the learner's answer, and gives a concrete next exercise. Confidence grows from a usable loop, not certainty theater.
posts.cta: Evaluate the feedback loop with a free practice attempt.
posts.assetBrief: Three-column visual: evidence, practice estimate, next exercise. No official exam branding.

posts.sourceConsentRequirement: Use fictional answers and clearly hypothetical practice scores. Real score comparisons require written learner consent, exact context, and approval of every slide.
posts.disclosure: Label all attempts and scores 'Illustrative practice example — not an official IELTS score'.
posts.hook: A higher retry score is useful only if you know what changed.
posts.caption: Compare the evidence: fewer restarts, clearer development, more precise words, or stronger stress. A practice estimate is not a prediction of an exam band.
posts.cta: Use one category to plan your next retry.
posts.assetBrief: Six slides compare fictional attempt evidence without testimonials or guaranteed improvement language.

posts.sourceConsentRequirement: No customer claim is used. A real school pilot result requires contract permission, institution approval, appropriate learner consent, and a documented methodology.
posts.disclosure: Present as a suggested pilot framework, not a customer case study.
posts.hook: Pilot the speaking workflow before you scale the licence.
posts.caption: Choose one cohort, one teacher workflow, one practice objective, and one adoption review. A smaller pilot gives schools evidence for the rollout decision without inventing certainty upfront.
posts.cta: Request a walkthrough focused on your cohort.
posts.assetBrief: Five-step pilot framework with no fabricated logos, metrics, or testimonials.

posts.sourceConsentRequirement: No learner source is used. Presenter rights and exam-accuracy review are required.
posts.disclosure: Independent preparation advice; avoid medical or guaranteed performance claims.
posts.hook: The night before: stop collecting new speaking templates.
posts.caption: Review your familiar answer structure, speak one calm warm-up, prepare logistics, and finish. Last-minute template hunting can crowd out the routine you already practiced.
posts.cta: Save this for your final preparation day.
posts.assetBrief: Calm checklist video: structure, warm-up, logistics, stop.

posts.sourceConsentRequirement: No learner source is used. Any added progress screenshot must use fictional data or written, purpose-specific learner consent.
posts.disclosure: Frame as a suggested routine, not a promised score trajectory.
posts.hook: Your four-week speaking loop, in seven slides.
posts.caption: Week 1 diagnose. Week 2 reduce fluency friction. Week 3 improve development and precision. Week 4 strengthen delivery and repeat. Keep one scored answer and one retry at the center of each week.
posts.cta: Start the loop with the free score diagnostic.
posts.assetBrief: Seven-slide recap with weekly actions and a final free-practice CTA.
